description: Round red silk lantern with gold end caps and a tassel, hung in pairs and rows over Chinese shopfronts and shrines

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Round hanging lantern, its body a plump barrel shape wider than it is tall with shallow vertical ribbing pressed into the surface, closed off top and bottom by broad flat circular end caps, a short stiff loop standing up from the top cap to hang it by, and beneath the bottom cap a single thick short tassel hanging as one solid tapered bundle with a small collar where it meets the cap Materials: Deep pillar-box red silk gone slightly uneven and sun-faded on one side, gold painted end caps with the paint worn thin at the rim, a gold character panel on the body, dust settled along the top cap, tassel frayed and dulled at its ends.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.925 carried from the recorded review; the rope added 472 triangles and one material. 1544/4000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Measured bbox 0.388 x 0.926 x 0.388 m against the declared 0.38 x 0.92 x 0.38 -- the height re-declared from 0.62 to 0.92 on the owner's brief (2026-09-03) because the prop now ships WITH a 0.30 m hanging cord; the fixture itself is unchanged at 0.62 (cap to tassel tip) and sits at y -0.92..-0.30 under the loop's crown at the origin. Width within 2%.

A plump barrel sampled by angle, r 0.19 at the equator closing to 0.072 at both caps, sixteen stitched seams as a ribbedDome modulation tinted toward the darker seam tone at the troughs. Unchanged; shifted down 0.30 with the fixture.

A gilt cap and collar at BOTH ends of the silk and the tassel of bound cord and tapering tuft below the lower cap, unchanged. The 5 mm wire hook above the top cap is replaced by a gold EYELET (r 0.012-0.015) the rope rises out of.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's gold character panel on the belly is still not carried (a placed decal, not a tile).

featureReviews.evidence: Three material layers now: the red silk at authored luma 37 (rendering near 48, clear of the erased 55.5-60.5 window at roughness 0.92), the gilt at 178 rendered, and a JUTE ROPE material (#b09f7c, the Lanna lantern's tone) with a 256 px laid-strand tile on culm UVs so the strands run along the cord and round the loop.
featureReviews.notes: The cord is an owner addition the plate does not show (it hangs on a bare wire there); tone carried from a probed sibling rather than measured on this plate.

name: Red Chinese Hanging Lantern
notes:
The Yaowarat and Chinese-shrine lantern, hung in pairs beside a door and in long rows under an awning, so it is placed in tens and must stay a single cheap volume. Sized as a 0.38 m body with the tassel bringing the whole hang to 0.62 m -- the height figure is the fixture plus tassel, not the cord, because the cord belongs to whatever it hangs from. The tassel is authored as one solid tapered bundle rather than loose strands deliberately: fringed geometry is exactly what the reference reconstruction loses and what costs a low-end GPU its frame. Pivot is top-center so it hangs from the fixing loop. Static: hung, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
